people.role: Democratic activist, former DPP chairman, Taiwan independence leader
facts: Born 1919 in Kaohsiung, Taiwan; died April 8, 2022
Political science professor at National Taiwan University
Leader of Taiwan's democratic independence movement
Co-authored 'Taiwan Self-Salvation Movement Manifesto' in 1964 with Hsieh Chun-min and Wei Ting-chao
All three were arrested and imprisoned for the manifesto
Escaped to Sweden in 1964 using a forged passport, then to the United States
Settled at University of Michigan's Center for Chinese Studies
Founding chairman of the Democratic Progressive Party (1986)
Ran for president in 2000, losing to Chen Shui-bian
Advocated for Taiwan independence, UN membership, and a new constitution
Wrote 'The World Changed' essay series
Mentored Yang Jia-you (Charles Yang) and other Taiwanese American activists
His escape involved changing identity and fleeing through Germany to Sweden
Remained on the Chinese blacklist for decades
Remembered as a teacher, friend, and tireless advocate for Taiwan's freedom
people.notes: Profile written by 楊嘉猷 (Charles Yang). Died 2022. Major figure in Taiwan's democratic movement.

facts: Ran '十全藥局' (Shiquan Pharmacy) in San Francisco for 30 years

Patients came from diverse backgrounds, ages, and genders
Discussed health issues, life difficulties, and personal problems
Maintained optimistic outlook despite physical disabilities
Refused to perform alone due to concerns about his condition
His radio program was popular with the community
